out_of_schema_notes: The finding, the root cause and its contributing cause, the remedy rule, the sample-size calculation, the model selection procedure, the impact assessment, the effectiveness check and the closure have no schema model; they are report_sections statements, one section per top-level section of the document. Each row of the chronology, scope, remedy, sample-size, power, augmentation-check, measured-results, impact, criteria, sensitivity and CAPA tables is a statement anchored on its own row. Where a continuation row reads exactly like another one (two remedy rows, two power rows), the statement also cites the row that opens its merged group.

Every model the document prints is a StatisticalModelFit: the full quadratic of the planned runs (Table 3, as Version 1.0 fitted it, Protein A run 23 at its design pH) and, from the prose, the same model of pool host cell protein with run 23 at its recorded pH; the model selected under corrective action CA3 for every output (Table 9); the selected models of the three augmented outputs on the planned runs and on all runs (Table 10, with their terms); and, from the prose, the full quadratic with a block term on all runs that each augmentation was sized for. The schema has no field for R² minus predicted R², the number of terms or the scale; they are in model_form and adequacy_statement. Numeric fields carry the values as printed; a p-value printed as '<0.001' or 'n.t.' is empty.

The model-adequacy finding is the Deviation record INV-002 (the investigation itself, as INV-001 records itself). DEV-005-01, the deviation of PCR-005 that INV-002 cites for Protein A run 23, is a second Deviation record. The plan discrepancies the document names (PD-003-02, PD-003-03, PD-005-02, PD-005-03, PD-005-04, PD-006-04, PD-007-01, PD-008-01, PD-008-02, PD-009-01) have no schema record; they are in the document relationships to the reports that record them and in the statements of the impact table.

studies holds the six planned response-surface designs (one per row of the scope table, with their runs and centre points; the study ids are those of the chronology) and the two D-optimal augmentations, each anchored on its chronology rows, its prose and every row of its design table. The augmentation is a second block of the response-surface design and has no study type of its own; it carries no n_runs, which the corpus test reserves for the seeded screening and response-surface designs, and its run count is in design_name. Only the augmentation design tables name every factor of a design, so only the augmentation records carry factors.

acceptance_criteria holds the criteria in force that the document prints: the five of the sensitivity table, the four judged on measured results, and the platform claim of low-pH viral inactivation for XMuLV clearance. The criteria 'without model selection' are what a verification on the full quadratic models would have given and were never in force; they are in the statements of the criteria and sensitivity tables. INV-002 prints no criteria-change table, so it has no superseded record. The QualityAttribute records list the same criteria and the drug substance limits the document states; their attribute_type comes from the CQA register, which INV-002 does not restate.

The proven acceptable range the document reports as moving (the lower end of elution buffer pH for pool host cell protein, in force and without model selection) is a statement and a row of the sensitivity table, not a ProvenAcceptableRange: the document gives its lower end only.

Parameters have no register in INV-002 and no ProcessParameter record. The parameter effects it states are assertions on the row or clause that states each: the terms of the selected models of all runs of the augmented outputs (Table 10), the fold changes of pool host cell protein (§8.2), the terms of the aggregate model of low-pH viral inactivation (§8.4) and the main effects of its XMuLV model (§9.2).

deviations.summary: Of the 22 full quadratic response-surface models that carry an acceptance criterion at their step, 14 did not meet the limit on overfitting of PCMP-001 §7.2, which allows predicted R² to fall short of R² by at most 0.20, and the model of acidic variants at low-pH viral inactivation reproduced every run exactly, so none of the three tests the investigation applies could be applied to it.
deviations.detected_during: Re-analysis of the response-surface models against the model-adequacy criteria of PCMP-001 Version 2.0
deviations.disposition: Classified minor and closed on 2026-09-28. Under the remedy rule approved on 2026-09-02, the production bioreactor design was augmented by 16 runs for high mannose and acidic variants and the anion exchange design by 12 runs for host cell protein (corrective action CA1), and the other failing models were refitted (CA2); model selection then replaced the refits for every response-surface output (CA3). The re-evaluation on all runs of CA1, the application of CA3 in the Version 2.0 reports and the preventive actions were open at closure.
deviations.impact_statement: No product impact: no batch was dispositioned on these models, and the Version 1.0 documents were on hold for BLA use.
